title: Retail Installment Contracts: Repossessed, Reinstated, Liquidated and Charged-Off Statuses
content:
**Following the recovery file.** On Retail Installment Contracts, the contract's default statuses follow the recovery file: the contract becomes repossessed on the date the repossession case records the vehicle as recovered, returns to active when the repossession case closes as reinstated, becomes paid off when it closes as redeemed and becomes liquidated when the vehicle is sold.

**While repossessed.** The contract accrues simple interest but carries no late charges, no extensions, no due-date changes and no ancillary charges.

**On reinstatement.** The next due date moves to the first due date after the reinstatement date, because the reinstatement amount pays every installment due through that date, and ordinary servicing resumes with the same scheduled payment, due day and final installment date.

**Charge-off.** An active contract that reaches the product's charge-off threshold in days past due, with no repossession case in pre-repo review, assigned or recovered status, is charged off on that day. A charged-off contract keeps its balance and accepts payments and payoff quotes, but is not eligible for extensions, due-date changes or reinstatement to active status. Days past due are the calendar days from the next due date to the day measured when the next due date is earlier, and 0 otherwise.

| Repossession case event | Contract status |
|---|---|
| vehicle recorded as recovered | repossessed |
| case closes as reinstated | active |
| case closes as redeemed | paid off |
| vehicle sold | liquidated |

**Hypothetical case.** A contract whose due day is the 12th is reinstated on 20 August; its next due date becomes 12 September, the first due date after the reinstatement date. A second active contract reaching the charge-off threshold while its repossession case is in assigned status is not charged off on that day.
